purpose: Explain and exactly solve the mutation-sensitive four-edge-cut atom exposed by v6.8. Each side is K5 with two independent edges deleted. Its four boundary vertices form two forced-equality colour wires, and every bijective four-edge gluing falls into one of two classes: pair-preserving gluings are 3-colourable, while pair-mixing gluings are impossible.

gadget.graph: K5 minus the two nonedges p0-p1 and q0-q1.
gadget.wire_theorem: Every proper 3-colouring satisfies col(p0)=col(p1)=a, col(q0)=col(q1)=b with a!=b, and col(h) equal to the unique third colour. Conversely every ordered pair of distinct colours (a,b) extends uniquely to the hub. Hence the gadget has exactly six proper 3-colourings and its boundary relation is exactly EQ(p0,p1) AND EQ(q0,q1) AND NEQ(p0,q0).
gadget.proof: The hub h is adjacent to all four boundary vertices. Each q-vertex is adjacent to both p-vertices and vice versa. If p0 and p1 differed, then together with h they would use all three colours, leaving no colour for q0. Therefore p0=p1; symmetrically q0=q1. The two classes are adjacent, so their colours differ, and h is forced to the third colour.

two_gadget_gluing.setup: Take two disjoint copies L,R of the gadget and connect their four boundary vertices by an arbitrary perfect matching, encoded as a bijection pi from the four L terminals to the four R terminals.
two_gadget_gluing.count_matrix: Collapse each side's two equality pairs to wire classes P,Q. Let M_pi be the 2x2 matrix whose entry M_ij counts matching edges from left wire class i to right wire class j. Every row and column sum is two.
classification: PAIR_PRESERVING: M is [[2,0],[0,2]] or [[0,2],[2,0]]. There are 4+4=8 terminal bijections of this type. The glued graph has exactly 18 proper 3-colourings.
PAIR_MIXING: M is [[1,1],[1,1]]. There are 16 terminal bijections of this type. The glued graph has no proper 3-colouring.

theorem.name: FOUR_CUT_EQUALITY_WIRE_GLUE_DICHOTOMY
proof: Write left wire colours as a,b with a!=b and right wire colours as c,d with c!=d.
For pair-preserving M, the matching inequalities are either a!=c and b!=d, or a!=d and b!=c. These constraints have exactly 18 ordered quadruples (a,b,c,d); both hubs are then uniquely forced.

For pair-mixing M, each left wire class has one edge to each right wire class. Hence a differs from both c,d and b also differs from both c,d. Because c,d are distinct in a three-colour palette, both a and b must equal the unique third colour, contradicting a!=b.
The 24 bijections of four terminals partition into 8 pair-preserving and 16 pair-mixing bijections, so the classification is exhaustive.

v6_8_explanation.negative_reassembly: The negative graph's four cut edges induce M=[[1,1],[1,1]], so it is rejected by the pair-mixing terminal.
v6_8_explanation.positive_reassembly: The balanced mutation changes the gluing to a pair-preserving matrix, so the positive graph has exactly 18 colourings.
v6_8_explanation.meaning: The minimal information lost by the transition matroid in this control is the pairing of boundary half-edges relative to the two forced-equality wire classes.

positive: A constant-time exact solve/contraction for this entire four-edge-cut gadget family.
A concrete mutation-sensitive boundary datum that restores the decision bit on the v6.8 control without enumerating 3^10 colourings.
An explicit example of how small boundary colour relations can be more informative for 3-COLOR than a mutation-invariant matroid representation.
firewall: Recognizing or computing an arbitrary large side's exact four-terminal colour relation is not assumed polynomial; the terminal applies only when the side is proved to be this gadget or another separately solved boundary class.
This does not solve pure essentially-six-edge-connected 4-regular Hamiltonian cores and does not imply that all balanced mutations reduce to a two-wire rule.

next_target.name: E8_MUTATION_SENSITIVE_BOUNDARY_RELATION_LIBRARY_OR_6EDGE_CORE_V7_0
next_target.directive: Use exact constant-boundary terminals only for source-recognizable solved pieces; do not assume arbitrary boundary relations are cheap to compute. In parallel, attack the essentially-six-edge-connected 4-regular Hamiltonian core where balanced-mutation decomposition is unavailable. Any proposed global invariant must distinguish the v6.8 mutation pair whenever a four-cut is present and must still make progress when no such cut exists.
